text:
rivka: Quick flag - dashboard p99 jumped to ~700ms for /v1/complete at 11:05 but the endpoint breakdown p99 is ~240ms. anyone else seeing mismatch?
sam: Yeah I saw that. Could be sample origin differences or retries counting.
joel: We recently changed endpoint slice defaults to hide proxy-origin by default, aggregate keeps it.
tanya: Can we confirm with a query?
joel: Ran this: `SELECT percentile(latency_ms,99) AS p99, sample_origin, count(*) FROM telemetry.samples WHERE endpoint='/v1/complete' AND time >= '2026-03-22T11:00Z' AND time <= '2026-03-22T11:10Z' GROUP BY sample_origin;` Gives proxy p99 ~712ms (200 samples), server p99 ~238ms (1800 samples).
sam: That explains it. Also ops logs show a short routing bump:
deploy-bot: rollout: canary/2026-03-22.11 applied to eu-central at 11:02
ravika: So fallback/proxy-heavy traffic hit the aggregate. UX issue: console didn't surface provenance on the p99 sparkline so it looked like a regression in backend.
joel: Proposal: add a tiny provenance pill next to percentile numbers and include origin counts in hover. Also add an "exclude retries" toggle (retry_count>0) in percentile queries.
tanya: Agreed. I'll draft a docs blurb explaining why p50/p95/p99 can differ across slices (origins, retries, routing fallback, cache hits).
sam: I can ship a small console patch for badge + tooltip this sprint. joel: I'll add the include-retries param to the telemetry API and return origin counts.
rev: Filing incident note: root cause = canary fallback weight + differing default provenance between aggregate vs endpoint slice. low-risk UX + API fixes planned.
